chunks: And by his chain, from Yunus, from the one who reported it, from Zurara, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) has said:
The married man (muhsan) would be stoned, and the one who had a slave girl and did not copulate with her, so (his punishment is) whipping of one hundred lashes and exile for a year.

key_terms.أُمْلِكَ: umlik — to be given possession/ownership; here refers to having a slave girl (jariya) given into one's possession
key_terms.الْمُحْصَن: muhsan — a person who is 'guarded' or 'protected' through a valid, consummated marriage; carries the maximum hadd penalty for zina
key_terms.جَلْد: jald — flogging/whipping; the hadd punishment for zina by a non-muhsan free person
key_terms.نَفْي: nafi — exile/banishment; additional punishment alongside flogging for the non-muhsan
key_terms.يُرْجَم: rajm — stoning to death; the hadd punishment for zina by a muhsan

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a married man (muhsan) who commits zina according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) distinguishes between two categories of fornication: the married man (muhsan) who is punished by stoning (rajm), and the man who possesses a slave girl but has not consummated the relationship and then commits fornication elsewhere, whose punishment is one hundred lashes and one year of exile. This hadith reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential understanding that the legal status of ihsan (being 'guarded' through a valid completed marriage) determines whether the hadd punishment is stoning or flogging combined with exile. The ruling on exile as a combined punishment for the non-muhsan male was a point of jurisprudential discussion among early Muslim scholars.
word_analysis: had a slave girl (was given possession of her)

en.hubeali:
And by his chain, from Yunus, from the one who reported it, from Zurara, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The married man would be stoned, and the one who had a slave girl and did not copulate with her, so whip him one hundred lashes and exile him for a year’.
